content: The text provided appears to be a list of references, primarily from the World Health Organization (WHO), detailing various guidelines, reports, and resources related to public health, mental health, reproductive health, child and adolescent health, and other medical topics. 1. The WHO's mhGAP Intervention Guide provides evidence-based recommendations for managing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in non-specialized healthcare settings. 2. The INSPIRE Handbook outlines actionable steps for implementing seven strategies aimed at ending violence against children. 3. The Adolescent Job Aid serves as a practical desk reference for primary-level health workers to address adolescent health needs effectively. 4. Sun protection is emphasized as a critical component of health-promoting schools, as outlined in WHO's school health document series. 5. WHO provides an information brief on promoting adolescent sexual and reproductive health through schools in low-income countries. 6. Guidance and recommendations are available from WHO to ensure human rights are upheld in the provision of contraceptive information and services. 7. The Global Health Sector Strategy on Sexually Transmitted Infections (2016–2021) outlines a roadmap toward ending STIs. 8. A practical handbook on school-based violence prevention offers strategies for creating safer educational environments. 9. WHO highlights the importance of fostering emotional and social well-being as a responsibility of health-promoting, child-friendly schools. 10. Guidelines are available for preventing early pregnancy and improving reproductive health outcomes among adolescents in developing countries. 11. Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations were updated in 2016. 12. WHO provides evidence-based behavior change techniques to promote mental health. 13. The World Report on Child Injury Prevention summarizes global efforts to reduce injuries among children. 14. A global call to action emphasizes the prevention of child and adolescent injuries. 15. WHO clinical and policy guidelines address responses to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. 16. A training resource on primary ear and hearing care is available for basic-level healthcare providers. 17. WHO provides fact sheets on deafness, hearing loss, blindness, and vision impairment, offering key information for public health awareness. 18. Strategies for preventing and managing childhood hearing loss are outlined in WHO resources. 19. Guidelines for hearing aids and services in developing countries were updated in 2004. 20. Healthy nutrition is identified as an essential element of health-promoting schools. 21. The Global Routine Immunization Strategies and Practices (GRISP) document complements the Global Vaccine Action Plan (GVAP). 22. WHO's position paper on vaccines against human papillomavirus (HPV) provides a summary of recommendations. 23. Updated recommendations for routine immunization are available in a user-friendly guide. 24. WHO's position paper on reducing pain during vaccination was published in September 2015. 25. A meeting report from WHO discusses autism spectrum disorders and other developmental disorders, focusing on raising awareness and building capacity. 26. The IMAI District Clinician Manual provides guidelines for managing illnesses in resource-limited settings. 27. WHO offers resources to improve the care of young children and support child development. 28. A global strategy aims to reduce the harmful use of alcohol through evidence-based interventions. 29. The mhGAP Mental Health Gap Action Programme focuses on scaling up care for mental, neurological, and substance use disorders. 30. WHO provides guidelines for managing stress-related conditions, particularly in emergency settings. 31. Psychological first aid guidelines are available for field workers responding to trauma and emergencies. 32. WHO offers psychosocial interventions for treating behavioral disorders in children. 33. Guidelines for the pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment of ADHD in children are provided by WHO. 34. WHO's guidelines on managing health complications from female genital mutilation aim to improve care for affected individuals. 35. The World Report on Disability (2011) highlights global challenges and strategies for improving the lives of people with disabilities. 36. WHO's Global Disability Action Plan (2014–2021) focuses on achieving better health for all individuals with disabilities. 37. Recommendations on adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights were published by WHO in 2018. 38. WHO provides antenatal care recommendations to ensure a positive pregnancy experience. 39. Standards for improving the quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities are outlined in WHO resources. 40. WHO guidelines address the treatment of sexually transmitted infections, including syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydia, and gonorrhea. 41. WHO provides comprehensive guidelines for the management of severe acute malnutrition in infants and children. 42. A guidance note from WHO emphasizes comprehensive cervical cancer prevention and control strategies. 43. Recommendations for isoniazid preventive therapy for individuals living with HIV in high TB and HIV prevalence settings were updated in 2015. 44. WHO guidelines on post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV and the use of co-trimoxazole prophylaxis for HIV-related infections are available. 45. Daily iron supplementation guidelines for infants, children, adolescent girls, and adult women are provided by WHO. 46. WHO offers guidance on the use of multiple micronutrient powders for food fortification in young children. 47. Caregiver skills training is available for managing developmental disorders in children. 48. WHO provides guidelines for managing diarrhea and pneumonia in HIV-infected infants and children. 49. A training guide for recognizing neglected tropical diseases through skin changes is available for frontline health workers. 50. WHO guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of leprosy are accessible for healthcare providers. 51. WHO offers a guide for program managers on the eradication of yaws. 52. Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and control of dengue and malaria are available from WHO. 53. WHO provides recommendations for managing fever in peripheral healthcare settings. 54. National tuberculosis programs can refer to WHO's guidance on managing TB in children. 55. WHO offers resources for treating measles in children. 56. Consolidated guidelines on sexual and reproductive health and rights for women living with HIV are available. 57. WHO provides an integrated approach to the nutritional care of HIV-infected children. 58. WHO's guidelines on the use of safety-engineered syringes aim to improve injection safety in healthcare settings. 59. WHO guidelines address the pharmacological treatment of persistent pain in children with medical illnesses. 60. WHO provides a technical package for road safety to save lives and prevent injuries. 61. The World Report on Road Traffic Injury Prevention highlights strategies for reducing road traffic injuries globally. 62. WHO offers resources on burn prevention, including success stories and lessons learned. 63. The physical school environment is identified as a critical element of health-promoting schools. 64. WHO provides recommendations for managing common childhood conditions, including pneumonia, dysentery, and severe acute malnutrition. 65. WHO and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) offer a basic emergency care workbook for managing acute illnesses and injuries.
